HEB.P.3.1-6.text: Jesus Our Apostle and High Priest

HEB.P.11.4-7.text: The Faith of Abel, Enoch, Noah

HEB.P.11.8-19.text: The Faith of Abraham and Sarah

HEB.P.11.20-22.text: The Faith of Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph

HEB.1.1-3.text: God spoke through the prophets, and now through his Son

HEB.1.4-5.text: The Son is greater than the angels

HEB.1.6-7.text: God tells the angels to worship the Son

HEB.1.8-9.text: God calls the Son God and king forever

HEB.1.10-12.text: The Son made the earth and will never change

HEB.1.13-14.text: God honors the Son; angels serve believers

HEB.2.1-1.text: The writer urges believers to pay close attention

HEB.2.2-4.text: Believers must not neglect so great a salvation

HEB.2.5-6.text: The world to come is not given to angels

HEB.2.7-8.text: God put everything under man, but not yet seen

HEB.2.9-10.text: Jesus suffered death for everyone and now has glory

HEB.2.11-12.text: Jesus is not ashamed to call believers his brothers

HEB.2.13-15.text: Jesus shared human life to free people from fear of death

HEB.2.16-18.text: Jesus became like his brothers to help the tempted

HEB.3.5-6.text: Moses was a servant; Christ is the Son over God’s house

HEB.3.7-8.text: The Holy Spirit warns believers not to harden their hearts

HEB.3.9-11.text: God was angry with Israel in the wilderness

HEB.3.12-13.text: Believers must encourage each other daily

HEB.3.14-15.text: Believers share in Christ if they hold firm to the end

HEB.3.16-19.text: Israel could not enter God’s rest because of unbelief

HEB.4.1-2.text: The promise of God’s rest still stands for believers

HEB.4.3-5.text: Believers enter God’s rest; God rested on the seventh day

HEB.4.6-7.text: God speaks through David about entering his rest today

HEB.4.8-11.text: A Sabbath rest remains; believers must work to enter it

HEB.4.12-13.text: God’s word is living and judges the heart

HEB.4.14-16.text: Believers can come to Jesus the high priest with confidence

HEB.5.1-3.text: A high priest offers sacrifices for sins of the people

HEB.5.4-5.text: God called Christ to be high priest, as he called Aaron

HEB.5.6-6.text: God says Christ is a priest like Melchizedek

HEB.5.7-8.text: Jesus prayed with tears and learned obedience by suffering

HEB.5.9-10.text: Jesus became the source of salvation and a high priest

HEB.5.11-11.text: The writer says the believers are slow to understand

HEB.5.12-14.text: Believers should be teachers but still need milk

HEB.6.1-3.text: Believers should leave basic teachings and grow mature

HEB.6.4-6.text: Those who fall away after knowing God cannot be restored

HEB.6.7-8.text: Useful land is blessed, but land with thorns is burned

HEB.6.9-10.text: God will not forget the believers’ work and love

HEB.6.11-12.text: The writer urges believers to be diligent and patient

HEB.6.13-15.text: God promised Abraham with an oath, and Abraham waited

HEB.6.16-18.text: God made an oath to give believers strong hope

HEB.6.19-20.text: Hope is an anchor, and Jesus is high priest forever

HEB.7.1-3.text: Melchizedek was a king and priest who blessed Abraham

HEB.7.4-6.text: Abraham gave a tenth to the great Melchizedek

HEB.7.7-10.text: Melchizedek is greater than Abraham and Levi

HEB.7.11-12.text: Another priest was needed, so the law must change

HEB.7.13-14.text: Jesus came from the tribe of Judah, not from priests

HEB.7.15-17.text: Jesus is a priest forever by the power of an endless life

HEB.7.18-19.text: The weak old law is replaced by a better hope

HEB.7.20-21.text: God made Jesus a priest with an oath

HEB.7.22-24.text: Jesus lives forever, so his priesthood has no end

HEB.7.25-26.text: Jesus always lives to save and speak for believers

HEB.7.27-28.text: Jesus offered himself once, unlike the other high priests

HEB.8.1-2.text: Believers have a high priest who serves in heaven

HEB.8.3-5.text: Jesus serves in heaven; earthly priests serve in a copy

HEB.8.6-7.text: Jesus brings a better covenant with better promises

HEB.8.8-9.text: God promises a new covenant to Israel and Judah

HEB.8.10-10.text: God will write his laws on the hearts of his people

HEB.8.11-12.text: Everyone will know God, and God will forgive sins

HEB.8.13-13.text: The new covenant makes the first covenant old

HEB.9.1-2.text: The first covenant had rules for worship and a tabernacle

HEB.9.3-5.text: The Most Holy Place held the ark and other sacred things

HEB.9.6-7.text: Only the high priest entered the second room, once a year

HEB.9.8-10.text: Old sacrifices could not cleanse the worshiper’s conscience

HEB.9.11-12.text: Christ entered the greater tabernacle by his own blood

HEB.9.13-15.text: Christ’s blood cleanses us and brings a new covenant

HEB.9.16-17.text: A will takes effect only after the one who made it dies

HEB.9.18-20.text: Moses sprinkled blood on the scroll and the people

HEB.9.21-22.text: Without blood there is no forgiveness of sins

HEB.9.23-24.text: Christ entered heaven itself to appear before God for us

HEB.9.25-26.text: Christ offered himself once for all to remove sin

HEB.9.27-28.text: Christ will come again to save those who wait for him

HEB.10.1-4.text: The law’s sacrifices could not make worshipers perfect

HEB.10.5-7.text: Christ came into the world to do God’s will

HEB.10.8-10.text: Christ’s one sacrifice replaces the old sacrifices

HEB.10.11-14.text: Christ offered one sacrifice and sat down at God’s right hand

HEB.10.15-16.text: God promises to put his laws in believers’ hearts

HEB.10.17-18.text: God will not remember sins, so no offering is needed

HEB.10.19-22.text: Believers can enter God’s presence through Jesus’ blood

HEB.10.23-25.text: Believers should hold on to hope and encourage each other

HEB.10.26-27.text: Believers who keep sinning on purpose face judgment

HEB.10.28-29.text: Those who reject the Son of God deserve worse punishment

HEB.10.30-31.text: God will judge his people, which is fearful

HEB.10.32-34.text: Believers endured suffering and loss with joy

HEB.10.35-37.text: Believers need to persevere to receive God’s promise

HEB.10.38-39.text: Believers live by faith and do not shrink back

HEB.11.4-4.text: Abel offered God a better sacrifice by faith

HEB.11.5-6.text: Enoch pleased God; without faith no one can please God

HEB.11.7-7.text: Noah built an ark by faith to save his family

HEB.11.8-10.text: Abraham went by faith and lived in tents as a stranger

HEB.11.11-12.text: Sarah trusts God’s promise and conceives a child

HEB.11.13-14.text: Believers of old died in faith as strangers on earth

HEB.11.15-16.text: Believers of old wanted a better, heavenly country

HEB.11.17-19.text: Abraham is ready to offer Isaac because he trusts God

HEB.11.20-22.text: The Faith of Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph

HEB.11.23-26.text: Moses chose to suffer with God’s people, not enjoy sin

HEB.11.27-28.text: By faith Moses left Egypt and kept the Passover

HEB.11.29-29.text: The people cross the Red Sea, but the Egyptians drown

HEB.11.30-31.text: Jericho’s walls fall and Rahab is saved by faith

HEB.11.32-34.text: Many people of faith won battles and shut lions’ mouths

HEB.11.35-38.text: Believers suffered torture, prison and death for faith

HEB.11.39-40.text: Believers of old and us will be made perfect together

HEB.12.4-6.text: Believers should not lose heart when God disciplines

HEB.12.7-8.text: Believers should endure suffering as God’s discipline

HEB.12.9-11.text: God’s discipline is painful but later brings peace

HEB.12.12-13.text: Believers must be strong and make straight paths

HEB.12.18-21.text: Believers have not come to a terrifying mountain

HEB.12.22-24.text: Believers have come to Mount Zion, the city of God

HEB.12.25-26.text: Believers must not refuse God, who speaks from heaven

HEB.12.27-29.text: Believers should worship God with reverence and awe

HEB.13.1-2.text: Believers should love each other and welcome strangers

HEB.13.3-4.text: Believers should remember prisoners and honor marriage

HEB.13.5-6.text: Believers should not love money and should trust God

HEB.13.7-8.text: Believers should remember leaders; Jesus never changes

HEB.13.9-11.text: Believers should not follow strange teachings about foods

HEB.13.12-14.text: Jesus suffered outside the city; believers follow him

HEB.13.15-17.text: Believers should praise God, do good and obey leaders

HEB.13.18-19.text: The writer asks the believers to pray for him

HEB.13.20-21.text: The writer prays that God will equip believers

HEB.13.22-23.text: The writer urges patience and tells about Timothy

HEB.13.24-25.text: The writer sends greetings and blessing to believers
